React compares values by identity to decide what to render again. If you change an object in place, it's still the same object, so React sees no change and the screen keeps showing the old data. Changing a prop also changes the parent's copy.

The rule reports assigning to a property, or using `delete` on one, when the property belongs to:

- props and the arguments of a hook
- a value returned by `useState`, `useContext`, and other hooks
- a value that was already passed to a hook or used in JSX
- a variable declared outside the component

It also reports a local variable that's reassigned after render, for example in an event handler.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react-hooks/immutability" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Price({ product }) {
  product.price = product.price / 2;
  return <span>{product.price}</span>;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
import { useState } from "react";

function Profile() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: "" });
  const rename = name => {
    user.name = name;
    setUser(user);
  };
  return <button onClick={() => rename("Ada")}>{user.name}</button>;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Box() {
  const style = { color: "red" };
  const box = <div style={style} />;
  style.color = "blue";
  return box;
}
```

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```jsx
import { useEffect } from "react";

const last = { title: "" };

function useTitle(options) {
  delete options.icon;
  last.title = options.title;
  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = options.title;
  });
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Counter() {
  let count = 0;
  const onClick = () => {
    count = count + 1;
  };
  return <button onClick={onClick}>{count}</button>;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Price({ product }) {
  const discounted = { ...product, price: product.price / 2 };
  discounted.label = "Sale";
  return <span>{discounted.label}: {discounted.price}</span>;
}
```

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { useState } from "react";

function Profile() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: "" });
  const rename = name => {
    setUser({ ...user, name });
  };
  return <button onClick={() => rename("Ada")}>{user.name}</button>;
}
```

The rule doesn't know what a method call does. This modifies the parent's array but isn't reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Tags({ tags }) {
  tags.push("new");
  return <span>{tags.length}</span>;
}
```
